newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: BK VISION FILES FURTHER UBS CHARGES.
newsitem.headline: BK VISION FILES FURTHER UBS CHARGES.

text.p: Investment trust BK Vision, part of Martin Ebner's BZ Group, has filed a further criminal charge against Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS), which Zurich's district attorney has combined with current investigations.

The latest charge specifically names UBS chairman Robert Studer, prompting prosecutors to name him as defendant and not just someone being questioned in the investigations, prosecutor Christian Weber said.

BK's latest charge accuses UBS of window-dressing earlier accounts and "untrue statements about their commercial activities" in connection with UBS' decision to take a special three billion Swiss franc provision in its 1996 accounts for future credit risk in the domestic loan portfolio.
In March 1995 BK Vision also brought criminal charges against the UBS chief executive and other responsible bodies, but these charges did not name Studer personally.
Since then prosecutors have been investigating the charges and Weber said it was still uncertain when he would decide whether or not to file charges against UBS with the courts.
Weber said the naming of Studer as defendant does not indicate the possible outcome of the prosecutor's investigation, but gives Studer certain legal rights.

In a statement Monday, UBS rejected BK Vision's charges of window-dresssing, saying the accounts had been prepared in conformity with internationally recognised accounting principles and certified by accountants.
"The board of directors's committee is confident that all these reasons weigh heavily enough for the proceedings to be dismissed," UBS said.
